# Aurora Robotics Inc. — Annual Report 2023

## Letter from the CEO

2023 was a challenging but important year for Aurora Robotics. We continued to grow revenue and our installed base, but we also faced two significant operational incidents that tested our engineering and customer support organizations. In September 2023, after eight years leading this company, Elena Marsh stepped down as CEO, and I was honored to be named her successor. I want to thank Elena for building the foundation this company stands on today, and I'm committed to continuing that work with the same focus on reliability and customer trust.

— Raj Patel, Chief Executive Officer

## Financial Highlights

Aurora Robotics Inc. reported total revenue of $71.2 million for fiscal year 2023, an increase of 21.3% over fiscal year 2022's revenue of $58.7 million. Despite continued revenue growth, the company recorded a net loss of $2.8 million for the year, driven by increased research and development spending, expansion costs in Austin, and approximately $420,000 in unplanned support costs related to the November 2023 firmware incident. Research and development spending grew to $15.9 million.

Headcount grew from 275 employees at the start of the year to 340 employees by December 31, 2023.

## Business Overview

2023 saw our Austin, Texas office reach full staffing levels, supporting both sales and an expanded field service organization across the central and southern United States.

The year was also marked by two operational incidents that are documented in detail in separate incident postmortems: a cloud dashboard outage in March 2023 caused by database connection pool exhaustion, and a firmware update incident in November 2023 that affected approximately 340 Falcon Drone v2 units in the field. Both incidents resulted in process changes described in their respective postmortem reports.

In Q3 2023, founding CEO Elena Marsh stepped down and was succeeded by Raj Patel, previously the company's Chief Operating Officer.

## Outlook

For 2024, management is prioritizing reliability and operational excellence following the incidents of 2023, alongside continued expansion of the Falcon Drone product line into new industrial verticals.
